thread:
sam: Quick design convo 1: we shipped the onboarding checklist drawer in prototype and the research folks say users miss the CTA. Thoughts on making progress more visible?

lia: Seen that. Maybe a small progress pulse anchored to the left nav (like 1/4 steps done) that expands into the drawer on click. Less intrusive than a full banner.

evan: Pulse is subtle but might be ignored. What if pulse pulses + a microcopy tooltip: "Complete setup (3 steps) -> Get to live inference". Clear intent.

tess: Concern: motion + screenreader. If pulse is animated, we need prefers-reduced-motion respect and no auto-announcements. Also it must be dismissible per user.

miguel: Metrics wise we want to measure CTA CTR and task completion. If we introduce pulse, add events: onboarding_pulse_shown, onboarding_pulse_clicked, checklist_completed_step.

sam: Good list. Another option: inline checklist collapsed in the Console home, with a compact header showing progress bar and a single CTA: "Finish setup (3 steps)". Click expands into step-by-step microflows.

lia: I like collapsed inline list for discoverability. Pulse + collapsed header might be redundant. Prefer one pattern. Which one scales to multi-org users?

evan: Collapsed inline is simpler for keyboard users. Pulse adds an extra DOM element and focus trap concerns. Plus tests showed people look at the page top-down, so inline will be seen.

tess: Accessibility checklist if we do inline collapsed list:
- Use <button aria-expanded> for expand/collapse
- When expanded, trap focus inside only if it's modal. For an inline panel do not trap focus.
- All interactive controls must be reachable via keyboard and have visible focus indicators
- Provide a skip link: "Skip onboarding steps" for power users

miguel: UX copy idea: change generic "Complete onboarding" to action-driven steps like "Connect API key", "Run your first request", "Import sample app". Microcopy should include estimated time per step (e.g., 1 min, 5 mins).

sam: Love that. Also suggest a tiny inline walkthrough for the "Run your first request" step: an inline terminal mock with a single prefilled curl/gpt call the user can copy. Low effort, high payoff.

lia: For sample apps, perhaps show 2 featured templates: "Chat demo (3 min)" and "Embedding search (5 min)" with thumbnail + tag "recommended". Don't overwhelm with too many choices.

evan: Implementation note: server should persist completed steps per user/org. Add API: POST /onboarding/v1/users/{id}/progress. Joel on infra can wire it. (tagging infra later)

tess: A11y small details:
- Contrast for progress text must be 4.5:1
- Use aria-live="polite" for progress updates when user completes a step
- Avoid auto-opening drawers on load (bad for screenreaders)

miguel: A/B test plan: Variant A = collapsed inline list, Variant B = left-nav pulse that expands. Track conversion to completed onboarding within 7 days. Add segment: new users vs returning.

sam: Who takes ownership? Lia can spec visuals, Evan can prototype the inline panel, Miguel sets up analytics + experiment, Tess will do a11y signoff. I'll coordinate with infra for persistence.

lia: I'll drop design frames by EOD tomorrow.

evan: I'll put a clickable Figma prototype up for testing by Thurs.

miguel: I'll sketch the GA events and experiment flags and link to feature flag in the experiment tracker.

tess: I'll draft the a11y QA checklist and run a quick keyboard-only pass once prototype ready.

ops-bot: Note: feature-flag entry required: ff_onboarding_progress_v1. Add to rollout queue before deploy.

sam: Great. I'll create the tech ticket and link designs. Thanks everyone :)
